title: FAILURE, REPAIR, NEXT VERSION
passages: My technical brain already understood iteration. Build something. Learn where it breaks. Refactor. Try again. I began using the same language for my life.

Failure could become information. Repair could become an action. I didn't need to pretend every disappointment had been useful or fair. I needed a way to respond that left me able to keep going. I started imagining the next version of myself as someone I could build through practice.

reflections.prompt: What is this version teaching you?
Think of one recent disappointment. What can you learn from it, and what is one repair you can make?
Choose one repair you can begin in ten minutes. Take the first step and note what happened.
